name: Active raised bogs
description: Acid bogs poor in mineral nutrients sustained mainly by rainwater.

name: Degraded raised bogs
description: Raised bogs where there has been disruption to the natural hydrology of the peat body.

name: Blanket bogs
description: Extensive bog communities or landscapes on flat or sloping ground with poor surface drainage.

name: Transition mires and quaking bogs
description: Peat-forming communities developed in low to moderately nutrient-rich water surfaces.

name: Depressions on peat substrates of the Rhynchosporion
description: Highly constant pioneer communities of the Rhynchosporion on humid exposed peat or sometimes sand.

name: Fennoscandian mineral-rich springs and spring fens
description: Springs and spring fens characterized by continuous flow of groundwater.

name: Calcareous fens with Cladium mariscus
description: Cladium mariscus beds of the emergent-plant zones of lakes or fallow lands or succession stage of extensively farmed wet meadows.

name: Petrifying springs with tufa formation
description: Hard water springs with active formation of travertine or tufa.

name: Alkaline fens
description: Wetlands mostly or largely occupied by peat or tufa-producing small sedge and brown moss communities.

name: Alpine pioneer formations
description: Alpine and peri-Alpine communities colonising neutral to slightly acid substrates soaked by cold water.

name: Aapa mires
description: Mire complexes in boreal zones characterised by minerotrophic fen vegetation in the central parts of the complexes.

name: Palsa mires
description: Subarctic mires where the climate is slightly continental and the mean annual temperature is below minus 1 degree Celsius.
